title: Serverless security: function permissions and dependencies

videos.script: A function has no server for you to patch. That part of the promise is true. {{edges}} But a function still has four edges, and every one of them is yours. {{role}} The first is what it may do. A function runs as a role, and any code inside it inherits that role. You will watch a role with every permission read a patient file it never needed. Then one line of policy takes that away. {{call}} The second is who may call it. A public address with no signature is an open door, however long the address is. {{secret}} The third is what it carries in its configuration. A password in an environment variable is readable by every read-only user. You will move it into Secrets Manager, and watch the analyst be refused. {{deps}} The fourth is what it carries in its package. The libraries inside were frozen the day it was built. An audit names the known flaws in them. A new pin, and a new package, clears them. {{end}}
